LESSON: READING 10.4.1 CHARACTERS AND THEIR TRAITS

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade seven
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 10
Topic 10.4: Reading 10.4.1 Characters and their traits
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Reading 10.4.1 Characters and their traits, part of Strand 10 in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade seven ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: What is the relevance of oral narratives in modern society?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. identify characters in monster narratives, (

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading 10.4.1 Characters and their traits in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. explain traits of characters in given monster narratives, (

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading 10.4.1 Characters and their traits in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. relate monster narratives to real life situations, (

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading 10.4.1 Characters and their traits in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. appreciate the importance of monster narratives in life.  Describe a monster/ ogre. Learners with speech difficulties could use alternative communication modes as they share their views. Allow more time for learners with speech difficulties to express their views.  Search online and offline for features of monster narratives. Adjust light intensity when using the digital device for learners with visual difficulties.  Narrate monster narratives from their immediate environment to their peers,  Discuss what monsters/ogres represent,  Discuss how monster narratives relate to real life,  Explain health education lessons they learn from monster narratives, 1. What is the relevance of oral narratives in modern society? 2. What should one consider when collecting narratives among people of varied socio-cultural backgrounds? 100  Dramatise a monster narrative and record the performance. SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Reading 10.4.1 Characters and their traits together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
 Critical thinking and problem solving are enhanced as the learner discusses the lessons learned and the relevance of monster

narratives in real life.

 Learning to learn is enhanced as the learner seeks support from resource persons on how to relate monsters to real life.

Values:
Patriotism is enhanced since the learner becomes conscious of their moral duties upon relating monster narratives to real life.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs)

Social awareness is enhanced when the learner relates monsters to real life.

Link to other subjects:

The learner relates the concept of characters and their traits to their learning of literary texts in Kiswahili.
